quote: none of the numbers ever came back worth shit
stewart_read: Customer discloses a prior negative solar-quote experience and the rep never asks which company or what the numbers showed.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged this an unrecoverable rabbit hole and prioritized re-booking speed — but no evidence of that reasoning is in the transcript.
coaching_implication: Probe: 'what was off about those numbers?' — turns a skepticism signal into a differentiation opening instead of ignoring it.

quote: I'm taking out a loan against my house, and the loan payment essentially is what you're balancing off of what my current electrical bill is?
stewart_read: This is a trust/scam-adjacent objection about financing mechanics; rep denies flatly instead of using it to reframe against the current bill.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep's 'No. No.' plus explaining financing options could be read as adequate transparency rather than a miss.
coaching_implication: Should flip to bill-pain framing: 'what's costing you is the bill you're already paying — this replaces that expense,' not just deny the loan characterization.

quote: We never actually got a chance to meet with you. We missed our appointments,
stewart_read: Rep skips straight into re-pitching without re-verifying homeowner status, interest reason, bill, or roof — none of the required verify items are asked.
alternative_hypothesis: This is a recycled/orphaned lead where some info may already be on file, which could justify compression per call_shape's note on context-justified compression.
coaching_implication: Even on a recycled lead, at minimum re-confirm interest reason before booking — none of that context exists in this call.

quote: because you're using electricity from the solar panels and not buying them from the electric company, we're able to get you a cheaper energy bill.
stewart_read: Rep explains the mechanics of how solar lowers a bill — closer-tier content — instead of redirecting to the specialist visit.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as necessary trust-building given the customer's financing suspicion, but it wanders into program mechanics beyond what's needed to book.
coaching_implication: Use the escape hatch: 'that's exactly what our specialist will walk through in the design' instead of explaining the savings mechanism.

quote: I can set a tentative appointment for next Saturday.
stewart_read: Customer self-offers only a tentative slot, not a firm commitment, and later reinforces the tentative framing at 02:34.
coaching_implication: Rep should have explicitly converted 'tentative' into a firm handshake ('is that fair?') rather than accepting the soft framing through to the end.

quote: we'll call you Friday the day before just to confirm with you. If you need to reschedule, not a problem.
stewart_read: Rep never runs the full button-up (no computer/no-driving instruction, no 'is that fair?' handshake) and pre-frames an easy reschedule path, weakening commitment.
coaching_implication: Lock the appointment with the full button-up script including the fairness handshake rather than pre-offering an easy out.
